title: Ravana proceeds to Mareecha
introduction: Ravana proceeds to Maareecha seeking his help in the abduction of Seetha. He travels by his aircraft-like chariot and on way he sees many locations along the seacoast that are affluent and divine. On seeing a banyan tree Ravana recollects the episode of Garuda, the Divine Eagle. He arrives at the hermitage of Maareecha.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे पंच त्रिंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 35th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः शूर्पणखा वाक्यम् तत् श्रुत्वा रोम हर्षणम् |
सचिवान् अभ्यनुज्ञाय कार्यम् बुद्ध्वा जगाम ह
verses.iast:
tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā vākyam tat śrutvā roma harṣaṇam |
sacivān abhyanuGYāya kāryam buddhvā jagāma ha
verses.translation: On hearing the exciting advise of Shuurpanakha then Ravana bade adieu to ministers, and indeed on resolving his further task he proceeded to his personal palace chambers.

glosses.meaning: that, Shuurpanakha's, sentence, advise, on hearing

verses.devanagari:
तत् कार्यम् अनुगम्यांतर् यथावत् उपलभ्य च |
दोषाणाम् च गुणानाम् च सम्प्रधार्य बल अबलम्
इति कर्तव्यम् इति एव कृत्वा निश्चयम् आत्मनः |
स्थिर बुद्धिः ततो रम्याम् यान शालाम् जगाम ह
verses.iast:
tat kāryam anugamyāṃtar yathāvat upalabhya ca |
doṣāṇām ca guṇānām ca sampradhārya bala abalam
iti kartavyam iti eva kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ |
sthira buddhiḥ tato ramyām yāna śālām jagāma ha
verses.translation: While following up his thinking about that task he got a pertinent thought, and on deliberating about the credits and discredits, strengths and weaknesses of that thought he decided that 'this is to be done in this method only.' On taking a decision in that way and with a firm mind he indeed proceeded to his excellent vehicle-garage.

glosses.meaning: strengths, weaknesses, on deliberating about - that thought
this task, be done this method
a decision, on making - on taking

glosses.itrans: tataH ramyaam yaana shaalaam jagaama ha
glosses.iast: tataḥ ramyām yāna śālām jagāma ha
glosses.devanagari: ततः रम्यां यान शालां जगाम ह
glosses.meaning: excellent, vehicle, garage, proceeded to, verily.

verses.devanagari:
यान शालाम् ततो गत्वा प्रच्छन्नम् राक्षस अधिपः |
सूतम् संचोदयामास रथः संयुज्यताम् इति
verses.iast:
yāna śālām tato gatvā pracchannam rākṣasa adhipaḥ |
sūtam sañcodayāmāsa rathaḥ saṃyujyatām iti
verses.translation: That lordly demon then has gone to the vehicle garage in secrecy, and directed the charioteer thus as, 'let the chariot be harnessed.'
notes: This 'secretly going to his own garage...' is one among the many oddities of Ravana that is suggested here. Kings never go to stables or garages but horses or chariots come to their fore, if ordered. Ravana's ministers have heard Shuurpanakha's report about the destruction of all the demons in Janasthaana. Because they have heard, it will not remain a secret or suppressible fact, but it will spread as a wild fire. Then some action has become necessary for Ravana now to save his face. prāṇam eva parityajya mānam eva abhirakśatu 'Let life go but not the self-respect...' So, his first thinking is to wage a war with Rama, but it may become a worthless expedition because Rama's capabilities are partially known. Next, he thought to abduct Seetha, for she is said not only to be beautiful but a dearly cherished wife of Rama. If Seetha is distracted from Rama, Rama may die anguishing for Seetha, thus this imminent danger, called Rama, gets ruined once for all.

The human nature isbhāryā duḥkham punar bhāryā just 'to lament for a parted wife for some time till a second wife is secured...' Thus, that wife-addict Rama will lament for Seetha for some time and seeks another woman as his wife. Instead, if he starts searching for Seetha alone, it is impossible for those two young humans to come searching this far, or to cross the ocean, or to enter Lanka. And even on entering Lanka, it is impossible to survive further at the hands of demons. These are some of the many of his deliberations on the 'strengths and weaknesses and the credits and discredits...' of his thought mentioned in the verse.

Then he enters his beautiful vehicle garage secretly. Why a king shall behave this quirkily? Because 'walls have ears...' and what all Shuurpanakha barked in the court must be audible throughout the palace by now, or may be all over Lanka, and if someone sees Ravana's exit at this point of time, everyone despises him, on the charge that he is trying to bring yet another woman. Though it is not said vividly here, that he is going to abduct Seetha thievishly keeping his valour and bravery aside, this will be made known in the words of Kumbhakarna in Yuddha Kaanda. This is shameful for his own self, as he did not do this way on previous occasions. For such a cowardly act, even Ravana's cherished wife Mandodari may despise or deride Ravana. So, he came to stables with a quirk of secrecy, which of course, will not remain a secret, soon.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः क्षणेन एव सारथिः लघु विक्रमः |
रथम् संयोजयामास तस्य अभिमतम् उत्तमम्
verses.iast:
evam uktaḥ kṣaṇena eva sārathiḥ laghu vikramaḥ |
ratham saṃyojayāmāsa tasya abhimatam uttamam
verses.translation: When that brisk-paced charioteer is said in this way he instantly harnessed the favourite and choicest chariot of Ravana with horses and got it ready.

glosses.meaning: thus, who is said - the charioteer
started to harness - horses, got it ready.

verses.devanagari:
कांचनम् रथम् आस्थाय कामगम् रत्न भूषितम् |
पिशाच वदनैः युक्तम् खरैः कनक भूषणैः
मेघ प्रतिम नादेन स तेन धनद अनुजः |
राक्षसाधिपतिः श्रीमान् ययौ नद नदी पतिम्
verses.iast:
kāṃcanam ratham āsthāya kāmagam ratna bhūṣitam |
piśāca vadanaiḥ yuktam kharaiḥ kanaka bhūṣaṇaiḥ
megha pratima nādena sa tena dhanada anujaḥ |
rākṣasādhipatiḥ śrīmān yayau nada nadī patim
verses.translation: That chariot which is decorated with golden ornaments, yoked with monster-faced mules that have gem studded trappings is rideable by the wish of the rider, and sitting in such a chariot which is wholly golden and which rides with a sound like the pealing of thunder, that celebrated Ravana, the brother of Kubera and the lord of demons, travelled towards the lord of rivers and rivulets, namely the ocean.

glosses.meaning: cloud, similar, with sound - pealing like a thunder

verses.devanagari:
स श्वेत वाल व्यजनः श्वेतः छत्रो दशाननः |
स्निग्ध वैदूर्य संकाश तप्त कान्चन भूषणः
दशग्रीवो विंशति भुजो दर्शनीय परिच्छदः |
त्रिदश अरिः मुनीन्द्र घ्नो दश शीर्ष इव अद्रि राट्
कामगम् रथम् आस्थाय शुशुभे राक्षसाधिपः |
विद्युन् मण्डलवान् मेघः स बलाक इव अंबरे
verses.iast:
sa śveta vāla vyajanaḥ śvetaḥ chatro daśānanaḥ |
snigdha vaidūrya saṅkāśa tapta kāncana bhūṣaṇaḥ
daśagrīvo viṃśati bhujo darśanīya paricchadaḥ |
tridaśa ariḥ munīndra ghno daśa śīrṣa iva adri rāṭ
kāmagam ratham āsthāya śuśubhe rākṣasādhipaḥ |
vidyun maṇḍalavān meghaḥ sa balāka iva ambare
verses.translation: Dasha-aanana, the decahedral demon, whose complexion like the smoothened Lapis-gem is lustrous, whose regalia that comprise white long-furred fans, white parasol and the like is spectacular, whose ornaments made out of refined gold are glittering, who similar to a kingly mountain with ten pinnacles and crags by way of his ten heads and twenty arms is gorgeous, and such a chief of demons who by that way is an adversary of gods and cutthroat of eminent-sages, seated in a nitid golden chariot that is rideable by the wish of its steersman, he shone forth like a black-cloud fringed with the streaks of lightning and rimmed with flights of cranes.
notes: Here the cloud metaphors with Ravana, the streaks of lightning with the silvery flashes of his regalia, and the decorated chariot with the flight of cranes.

glosses.meaning: [his body] smooth, Lapis, similar in shine
ten, heads [pinnacles,] mountain, king, who is similar to
by wish, rideable, chariot, seated in
one with lightning flashes, and with such an area around it

verses.devanagari:
स शैलम् सागर अनूपम् वीर्यवान् अवलोकयन् |
नाना पुष्प फलैर् वृक्षैर् अनुकीर्णम् सहस्रशः
verses.iast:
sa śailam sāgara anūpam vīryavān avalokayan |
nānā puṣpa phalair vṛkṣair anukīrṇam sahasraśaḥ
verses.translation: That dauntless Ravana forged ahead while viewing the area along the coastline which is interspersed with thousands of mountains and which is with variously flowered and fruited trees.

verses.devanagari:
शीत मंगल तोयाभिः पद्मिनीभिः समंततः |
विशालैः आश्रम पदैः वेदिमद्भिः अलंकृतम्
verses.iast:
śīta maṃgala toyābhiḥ padminībhiḥ samaṃtataḥ |
viśālaiḥ āśrama padaiḥ vedimadbhiḥ alaṃkṛtam
verses.translation: Everywhere the coastland is bedecked with lotus-lakes containing clean and cool waters, and with extensive thresholds of hermitages containing Fire-altars.

glosses.meaning: everywhere, bedecked with - seeing them he proceeded.

verses.devanagari:
कदल्य अटवि संशोभम् नालिकेर उपशोभितम् |
सालैः तालैः तमालैः च तरुभिः च सुपुष्पितैः
verses.iast:
kadalya aṭavi saṃśobham nālikera upaśobhitam |
sālaiḥ tālaiḥ tamālaiḥ ca tarubhiḥ ca supuṣpitaiḥ
verses.translation: Entire coast is gleaming with banana plantation and glistening with coconut trees, and the saala, palm, and tamaala trees are also in full blossom.

glosses.meaning: with banana, orchards - plantation, gleaming with

glosses.itrans: saalaiH taalaiH tamaalaiH ca tarubhiH ca supuSpitaiH
glosses.iast: sālaiḥ tālaiḥ tamālaiḥ ca tarubhiḥ ca supuṣpitaiḥ
glosses.devanagari: सालैः तालैः तमालैः च तरुभिः च सुपुष्पितैः
glosses.meaning: saala, palm, tamaala, trees, as well, well, blossomed.

verses.devanagari:
अत्यन्त नियत आहारैः शोभितम् परम ऋषिभिः |
नागैः सुपर्णैः गंधर्वैः किंनरैः च सहस्रशः
जित कामैः च सिद्धैः च चारणैः च उपशोभितम् |
आजैः वैखानसैः माषैः वालखिल्यैः मरीचिपैः
verses.iast:
atyanta niyata āhāraiḥ śobhitam parama ṛṣibhiḥ |
nāgaiḥ suparṇaiḥ gaṃdharvaiḥ kiṃnaraiḥ ca sahasraśaḥ
jita kāmaiḥ ca siddhaiḥ ca cāraṇaiḥ ca upaśobhitam |
ājaiḥ vaikhānasaiḥ māṣaiḥ vālakhilyaiḥ marīcipaiḥ
verses.translation: It is brightened up with thousands of reptiles and birds, with those many celestial beings that frequent the earth like gandharva-s, kinnaraa-s. And with eminent sages who have highly controlled food-habits, as well. It is also refulgent with the self-denying Siddha-s, Carana-s, and with sages that are the brainchildren of Brahma, namely Vaikhanasa-s, Maasha-s, Vaalakhilya-s, Mariicipa-s.
notes: The details about these sages are given in the 6th chapter of this Aranya Kanda when these categories of sages meet Rama requesting protection from demons.

glosses.meaning: kinnara's ca = with thousands of, kinnaraiH, as well
with Mariicipa-s, sages that dink moonbeams

verses.devanagari:
दिव्य आभरण माल्याभिः दिव्य रूपाभिः आवृतम् |
क्रीडा रति विधिज्ञाभिः अप्सरोभिः सहस्रशः
verses.iast:
divya ābharaṇa mālyābhiḥ divya rūpābhiḥ āvṛtam |
krīḍā rati vidhiGYābhiḥ apsarobhiḥ sahasraśaḥ
verses.translation: With thousands of celestial maidens divine in their mien, namely apsara-s, who are prettified with divine ornaments and garlands, and who are also the experts in the methodical sex-games that seaside is pervaded.

glosses.meaning: game of, sex, methods, experts in

verses.devanagari:
सेवितम् देव पत्नीभिः श्रीमतीभिः उपासितम् |
देव दानव सन्घैः च चरितम् तु अमृत अशिभिः
verses.iast:
sevitam deva patnībhiḥ śrīmatībhiḥ upāsitam |
deva dānava sanghaiḥ ca caritam tu amṛta aśibhiḥ
verses.translation: That seacoast is adored by the propitious wives of gods and frequented by the assemblages of gods who thrive upon ambrosia, and even patronised by demons that strive for ambrosia.
notes: The demons did not get their share of amR^ita 'divine elixir' therefore they cannot be called amR^ita ashibhiH 'ambrosia consumers.' As such, some other mms contain this expression amR^ita arthibhiH 'desirers of ambrosia...' the demons. They also frequent those coasts along with gods.

glosses.meaning: on ambrosia, thrive upon [or, who strive for]

verses.devanagari:
हंस क्रौन्च प्लव आकीर्णम् सारसैः संप्रणादितम् |
वैदूर्य प्रस्तरम् स्निग्धम् सांद्रम् सागर तेजसा
verses.iast:
haṃsa kraunca plava ākīrṇam sārasaiḥ sampraṇāditam |
vaidūrya prastaram snigdham sāṃdram sāgara tejasā
verses.translation: It is spread with swans, ruddy-gees and frogs, and there the waterfowls are very noisy, and stones overlain on the coast are like lapis-gems, and with the ambience of ocean that whole delta is appearing smooth and sludgy.

glosses.meaning: with swans, ruddy-gees, frogs, spread out
by saarasa water-fowls, very, much, noisy

verses.devanagari:
पाण्डुराणि विशालानि दिव्य माल्य युतानि च |
तूर्य गीत अभिजुष्टानि विमानानि समंततः
तपसा जित लोकानाम् कामगान् अभिसंपतन् |
गन्धर्व अप्सरसः चैव ददर्श धनदानुजः
verses.iast:
pāṇḍurāṇi viśālāni divya mālya yutāni ca |
tūrya gīta abhijuṣṭāni vimānāni samaṃtataḥ
tapasā jita lokānām kāmagān abhisampatan |
gandharva apsarasaḥ caiva dadarśa dhanadānujaḥ
verses.translation: While Ravana, the brother of Kubera, is quickly transiting he saw everywhere the whitish and widish aircrafts belonging to the deified souls who acquired higher worlds, and from those aircrafts adorned with divine flowery tassels and piloted by the wish of their steersmen, instrumental and vocal music is resonating, and gandharva-s are singing and apsara-s are dancing in them.

glosses.meaning: towards, quickly, falling - while quickly going
by asceticism, of those who acquired, [higher] worlds
= by wish, moving, aircrafts - of deified souls
gandharva-s, apsara-s, also thus - in those aircrafts, where gandharva-s are singing, and apsara-s are dancing

verses.devanagari:
निर्यास रस मूलानाम् चंदनानाम् सहस्रशः |
वनानि पश्यन् सौम्यानि घ्राण तृप्ति कराणि च
verses.iast:
niryāsa rasa mūlānām caṃdanānām sahasraśaḥ |
vanāni paśyan saumyāni ghrāṇa tṛpti karāṇi ca
verses.translation: Ravana proceeded while observing thousands of woodlands with sandalwood trees that are soothing and satisfying the sense of smell, and that oozed sweet-smelling resin at their bases.

glosses.meaning: sense of smell, satisfying to, also
in thousands, woodlands, while observing - Ravana proceeded.

verses.devanagari:
अगुरूणाम् च मुख्यानाम् वनानि उपवनानि च |
तक्कोलानाम् च जात्यानाम् फलानाम् च सुगन्धिनाम्
verses.iast:
agurūṇām ca mukhyānām vanāni upavanāni ca |
takkolānām ca jātyānām phalānām ca sugandhinām
verses.translation: He also observed on his way the forests and woodlands containing the noteworthy aloe plants, Takkola trees, and the nutmeg trees that are with fruits and aromatic, as well.

glosses.meaning: noteworthy, aloe vera plants, forests of
with fruits of, also, aromatic ones

verses.devanagari:
पुष्पाणि च तमालस्य गुल्मानि मरिचस्य च |
मुक्तानाम् च समूहानि शुष्यमाणानि तीरतः
verses.iast:
puṣpāṇi ca tamālasya gulmāni maricasya ca |
muktānām ca samūhāni śuṣyamāṇāni tīrataḥ
verses.translation: Also seen are the flowers of Tamaala trees, shrubberies of pepper, and heaps of desiccating pearl-oysters along the seashore.

glosses.meaning: of Tamaala trees - cassia, at flowers, also
of pearls [of oysters,] heaps, also - he saw.

verses.devanagari:
शैलानि प्रवरान् चैव प्रवाल निचयान् तथा |
कांचनानि च शृंगाणि राजतानि तथैव च
verses.iast:
śailāni pravarān caiva pravāla nicayān tathā |
kāṃcanāni ca śṛṃgāṇi rājatāni tathaiva ca
verses.translation: Thus, he saw the peaking boulders, like that the reefs of corals, and like that also at the mountains that have golden and silvern crests.

glosses.meaning: boulders, very best ones - peaking, also thus
conch shells, heaps of, also thus]
golden, silvern, also - suggesting their ores inside

verses.devanagari:
प्रस्रवाणि मनोज्ञानि प्रसन्नानि अद्भुतानि च |
धन धान्य उपपन्नानि स्त्री रत्नैः आवृतानि च
हस्ति अश्व रथ गाढानि नगराणि विलोकयन् |
verses.iast:
prasravāṇi manoGYāni prasannāni adbhutāni ca |
dhana dhānya upapannāni strī ratnaiḥ āvṛtāni ca
hasti aśva ratha gāḍhāni nagarāṇi vilokayan |
verses.translation: On seeing the delightful, serene, and marvellous cascades, and cities that are abundant in wealth and agricultural produce, and abundant with gemlike womenfolk, and that are replete with elephants, horses, and chariots, Ravana proceeded further.

glosses.meaning: cities, while viewing at - he proceeded.

verses.devanagari:
तम् समम् सर्वतः स्निग्धम् मृदु संस्पर्श मारुतम्
अनूपे सिन्धु राजस्य ददर्श त्रिदिव उपमम् |
verses.iast:
tam samam sarvataḥ snigdham mṛdu saṃsparśa mārutam
anūpe sindhu rājasya dadarśa tridiva upamam |
verses.translation: Ravana observed the delta adjacent to seacoast of that kingly ocean to be uniform and smooth, while the light air breezing in there is soft for touch, thus it looked heavenly.
notes: The demons did not get their share of amṛta'divine elixir' therefore they cannot be called amṛta aśibhiḥ'ambrosia consumers.' As such, some other mms contain this expression amṛta arthibhiḥ'desirers of ambrosia...' the demons. They also frequent those coasts along with gods.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र अपश्यत् स मेघ आभम् न्यग्रोधम् मुनिभिर् वृतम्
समंतात् यस्य ताः शाखाः शत योजनम् आयताः |
verses.iast:
tatra apaśyat sa megha ābham nyagrodham munibhir vṛtam
samaṃtāt yasya tāḥ śākhāḥ śata yojanam āyatāḥ |
verses.translation: There Ravana also saw a banyan tree which in sheen is like a black-cloud, and the branches of which are stretching all over for a hundred yojana-s in length, and on which sages made their abode for practising ascesis.

glosses.meaning: all over, hundred, yojana, in length
which tree is - cloudlike, in shine
with sages, encompassing it - sages settled on that tree practising ascesis
Indian Fig tree [banyan tree, Ficus benghalensis - the branches of which hang down and root themselves,]

verses.devanagari:
यस्य हस्तिनम् आदाय महा कायम् च कच्छपम्
भक्षार्थम् गरुडः शाखाम् आजगाम महाबलः |
verses.iast:
yasya hastinam ādāya mahā kāyam ca kacchapam
bhakṣārtham garuḍaḥ śākhām ājagāma mahābalaḥ |
verses.translation: This is the tree on the branch of which once highly mighty Divine Eagle Garuda swooped to perch, clawing an elephant and a mammoth tortoise, for the purpose of dining them out on that tree-branch.
notes: One yojana is 900 miles, where one yojana is nine English miles. The legendary version is that the elephant and tortoise are engaged in a fierce fight though none of them is a prey to the other, and seeing them and to teach a lesson to such causeless quarrellers, Garuda flies in and claws both and searches for a place to feast on them. Finding this tree worthwhile to have a leisure dinner he dashes on to one branch.

glosses.meaning: on to tree branch, arrived - swooped to perch.

verses.devanagari:
तस्य ताम् सहसा शाखाम् भारेण पतगोत्तमः
सुपर्णः पर्ण बहुलाम् बभंज अथ महाबलः |
verses.iast:
tasya tām sahasā śākhām bhāreṇa patagottamaḥ
suparṇaḥ parṇa bahulām babhaṃja atha mahābalaḥ |
verses.translation: While descending rapidly then that best bird among birds Garuda suddenly broke that tree's branch which is full with leaves, owing to the impact of his high impetuosity.

glosses.meaning: highly mighty - with high impetuous Garuda
one with - excellent, wings - Garuda, the eagle
that, with leaves, many - that branch full with leaves
owing to his weight, suddenly, broke - while descending rapidly.

verses.devanagari:
तत्र वैखानसा माषा वालखिल्या मरीचिपाः
अजा बभूवुः धूम्राः च संगताः परमर्षयः |
verses.iast:
tatra vaikhānasā māṣā vālakhilyā marīcipāḥ
ajā babhūvuḥ dhūmrāḥ ca saṃgatāḥ paramarṣayaḥ |
verses.translation: Adhering to that tree-branch there are eminent sages like, Vaikhanasa-s, Maasha-s, Vaalakhilya-s, Mariicipa-s, Aja-s, and even sages like Dhuumraa-s that thrive on fumes and smokes are there, and there they are collectively practising asceticism upside down while clasping branches with their legs.

verses.devanagari:
तेषाम् दयाअर्थम् गरुडः ताम् शाखाम् शत योजनाम्
भग्नम् आदाय वेगेन तौ च उभौ गज कच्छपौ |
verses.iast:
teṣām dayāartham garuḍaḥ tām śākhām śata yojanām
bhagnam ādāya vegena tau ca ubhau gaja kacchapau |
verses.translation: For the sake of the grace of those sages Garuda took flight from that tree, grasping that broken tree-branch of a hundred yojana length along with those pendulous sages with his beak, and both of the elephant and tortoise with both of his claws.

glosses.meaning: of hundred, yojana-length, that, broken, tree-branch
quickly, [he went - to relocate the sages - verse finishes later.]

verses.devanagari:
एक पादेन धर्म आत्मा भक्षयित्वा तत् आमिषम्
निषाद विषयम् हत्वा शाखया पतगोत्तमः |
प्रहर्षम् अतुलम् लेभे मोक्षयित्वा महामुनीन्
verses.iast:
eka pādena dharma ātmā bhakṣayitvā tat āmiṣam
niṣāda viṣayam hatvā śākhayā patagottamaḥ |
praharṣam atulam lebhe mokṣayitvā mahāmunīn
verses.translation: That virtue-souled Garuda consumed the meat of his prays, namely the elephant and the giant tortoise with a single foot, and destroyed the province of tribesmen with the same broken tree branch, and thus that supreme bird Garuda gained an incomparable happiness in rescuing those great-sages.
notes: Garuda held tortoise and elephant in two claws in the first instance and when to settle down on tree branch he transferred one pray from one claw to the other and held both of them by one claw and with the other free claw he caught hold of the tree branch. But it broke under his weight, and then suddenly without making it to fall on ground he grasped that branch with his beak and took to flight. While flying in sky he held both the preys in claw, and the tree branch into the other. Then he started to eat his preys in sky with one claw, still upholding the branch from falling. Seeing this feat of Garuda, the sages clinging to that tree branch bless him to be successful in his next mission and leave that branch. When that tree branch is free from sages, Garuda throws it on a province of some antagonistic tribal community, by weight of which the whole of that tribal community is destroyed. This is one way of telling the myth.

glosses.meaning: among birds, the best - supreme bird Garuda
great-sages, having released, rescued - in a safe place

verses.devanagari:
स तेन तु प्रहर्षेण द्विगुणी कृत विक्रमः |
अमृत आनयनार्थम् वै चकार मतिमान् मतिम्
verses.iast:
sa tena tu praharṣeṇa dviguṇī kṛta vikramaḥ |
amṛta ānayanārtham vai cakāra matimān matim
verses.translation: When his valour has become twice as much with that happiness that heedful Garuda indeed resolved to bring ambrosia from heaven.

glosses.meaning: with two, multiplied - double, rendered, valour - his valour became twice as much - as sages blessed for rescuing them
ambrosia, bringing - from heaven, for the purpose of, indeed

verses.devanagari:
अयो जालानि निर्मथ्य भित्त्वा रत्न गृहम् वरम् |
महेन्द्र भवनात् गुप्तम् आजहार अमृतम् ततः
verses.iast:
ayo jālāni nirmathya bhittvā ratna gṛham varam |
mahendra bhavanāt guptam ājahāra amṛtam tataḥ
verses.translation: Smashing the guard of iron-grid completely and crashing the unbreakable diamond -like strongroom in which the ambrosia is safeguarded, then Garuda carried off ambrosia from the palace of Indra.

glosses.meaning: unbreakable like - diamond, best - strong, room, on crashing

verses.devanagari:
तम् महर्षि गणैः जुष्टम् सुपर्ण कृत लक्षणम् |
नाम्ना सुभद्रम् न्यग्रोधम् ददर्श धनद अनुजः
verses.iast:
tam maharṣi gaṇaiḥ juṣṭam suparṇa kṛta lakṣaṇam |
nāmnā subhadram nyagrodham dadarśa dhanada anujaḥ
verses.translation: Ravana on his way saw such a banyan tree named as Subhadra which is a much sought after tree for assemblages of great sages, and which betokens the deeds of that best-winged Garuda.

glosses.meaning: at it [tree,] great-sages, by assemblages of, sought-after
by best-winged Garuda, deed, signs - betokens Garuda's actions
that, banyan tree, Ravana saw - and proceeded.

verses.devanagari:
तम् तु गत्वा परम् पारम् समुद्रस्य नदी पतेः |
ददर्श आश्रमम् एकांते पुण्ये रम्ये वनांतरे
verses.iast:
tam tu gatvā param pāram samudrasya nadī pateḥ |
dadarśa āśramam ekāṃte puṇye ramye vanāṃtare
verses.translation: On going to the other side of the lord of rivers, namely ocean, Ravana saw a pleasing hermitage in the sacred and scenic interior of the forest.

glosses.meaning: scenic, sacred, in forest, interiors of

verses.devanagari:
तत्र कृष्ण अजिन धरम् जटा वल्कल धारिणम् |
ददर्श नियत आहारम् मारीचम् नाम राक्षसम्
verses.iast:
tatra kṛṣṇa ajina dharam jaṭā valkala dhāriṇam |
dadarśa niyata āhāram mārīcam nāma rākṣasam
verses.translation: At that place Ravana saw the demon named Maareecha, wearing jute-clothes and black deerskin and tufts of hairs, and the one with regulated diet.

glosses.meaning: tufts of hair, jute-cloths, wearing one

verses.devanagari:
स रावणः समागम्य विधिवत् तेन रक्षसा |
मारीचेन अर्चितो राजा सर्व कामैः अमानुषैः
verses.iast:
sa rāvaṇaḥ samāgamya vidhivat tena rakṣasā |
mārīcena arcito rājā sarva kāmaiḥ amānuṣaiḥ
verses.translation: That demon Maareecha welcomed the king Ravana and customarily entertained him catering all the offerings that are beyond the scope of humans.

verses.devanagari:
तम् स्वयम् पूजयित्वा च भोजनेन उदकेन च |
अर्थोपहितया वाचा मारीचो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tam svayam pūjayitvā ca bhojanena udakena ca |
arthopahitayā vācā mārīco vākyam abravīt
verses.translation: On personally offering meals and drinking water, and venerating him properly Maareecha spoke this sentence to Ravana which is connotative of significance.

glosses.meaning: with meals, and with drinking water [offering]

verses.devanagari:
कच्चित् ते कुशलम् राजन् लंकायाम् राक्षसेश्वर |
केन अर्थेन् पुनः त्वम् वै तूर्णम् एव इह आगतः
verses.iast:
kaccit te kuśalam rājan laṃkāyām rākśaseśvara |
kena arthen punaḥ tvam vai tūrṇam eva iha āgataḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, king of the demons, is everything well with your Lanka? Oh, king, for what reason you have put in an appearance again, that too in a trice?
notes: This statement contains 'why you have come again?' and taking hold of this word, 'again...' some, who hold that the episode of Akampana is justifiable, say that the episode of Akampana is not interpolated but the original work of Valmiki. For this, the ex-party says that when a whole of chapter is included, inclusion of one word 'again...' is not a bothersome affair to the mythologists or interpolators. When it is questioned that interspersing Akampana's episode defeats the spectacular entry of Ravana, the defendants say that the antagonists need not be given such priorities. So also, Vali's Kishkindha is not portrayed in a spectacular way when Sugreeva attacked Vali for the first time, but it is detailed in the second round, to some extent, and fully when Lakshmana enters it.

In this episode, a jump of event to Garuda's exploits may be jerky, but it is questioned when can Ravana recollect about Garuda's might, why does he ignore still mightier Vishnu. Ravana's continuous fear for Vishnu made him to think of Garuda - that too, on seeing Subhadra, the banyan tree, and that too - while going to kidnap Seetha.

The path through which Ravana coursed is towards Himalayas, where an idolatry place called deva bhuumi is said to be earmarked for higher souls. When Rama hit Maareecha, he fell far off from the ritual place of Vishwamitra. That place is said to be on northern side of Himalayas. Some ancient mms contain this verse which also tell about that place as deva bhuumi and it is on the northern side of kuru i.e., kurukhsetra where Great War of Maha Bharata occurred: uttarānśca kurūn paśyan paśyan caiva nagottamān | deva dānava sanghaiḥ ca sevitam hi amṛta arthibhiḥ ||

glosses.meaning: in your, Lanka, safe, isn't it
again, in a trice, only, here, came.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तो महातेजा मारीचेन स रावण |
ततः पश्चात् इदम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत् वाक्य कोविदः
verses.iast:
evam ukto mahātejā mārīcena sa rāvaṇa |
tataḥ paścāt idam vākyam abravīt vākya kovidaḥ
verses.translation: When Maareecha spoke to him thus, that highly radiant and eloquent Ravana then afterwards spoke this sentence to Maareecha.

glosses.meaning: highly radiant one, sentence making, expert in - eloquent one
